question:
(i) A rectangular conducting loop is pulled out of a uniform magnetic field with constant speed $v$. Explain why an emf is induced in the loop.
(ii) If the side of the loop perpendicular to the motion has length $l$, obtain the expression for induced emf.
(iii) Calculate the induced emf when $B = 0.60\text{ T}$, $l = 0.30\text{ m}$ and $v = 2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

options.A:
(i) As the loop is pulled out, the area within the magnetic field and hence magnetic flux changes, inducing emf.
(ii) $\varepsilon=Blv$
(iii) $0.45\text{ V}$
options.B:
(i) An emf is induced because the magnetic field is steady, even though flux is unchanged.
(ii) $\varepsilon=\dfrac{Bv}{l}$
(iii) $5.0\text{ V}$
options.C:
(i) No emf is induced because the loop moves with constant speed.
(ii) $\varepsilon=0$
(iii) $0\text{ V}$
options.D:
(i) Flux increases as the loop leaves the field.
(ii) $\varepsilon=B\dfrac{l}{v}$
(iii) $0.072\text{ V}$
